question: What should the yogin contemplate, and how is channel-dissolution effected?
premises: Channel-dissolution, element-conquest, element-isolation, and element-separation are to be contemplated by the yogin.
Dissolution means merging the in- and out-breaths in the middle channel through long breath-retention practice.
As the cited Svacchanda passage teaches: exhaling by one path, filling by the other.
inference: Breath-merged channel-dissolution grounds the contemplations of conquest, isolation, and separation.
uncertainties: Svacchanda quote extent within the commentary.
plain_english: Channel-dissolution, element-conquest, element-isolation, and element-separation are to be contemplated by the yogin: the dissolution of the channels carrying in-breath and out-breath is their merging in the middle channel, in the fire of the up-breath, through long practice of breath-retention, as the cited Svacchanda passage teaches — exhaling by one path, filling by the other.
